objectives: Connect grapheme l to /l/ in taught CVC words.
Decode CVC words containing l by mapping each grapheme to its sound.
Blend /l/ with short vowels and taught final consonants.
concepts: Decoding follows the full grapheme-to-phoneme sequence.
Blending combines individual sounds into a spoken word.
Checking the middle vowel prevents common CVC substitutions.

definitions.definition: A letter or letter group used to represent a speech sound.
Combine individual phonemes smoothly to say a whole word.
Use grapheme-sound knowledge to read a printed word.

commonMistakes: Guessing from the first letter only.
Reading letter names instead of sounds.

basic: Decode taught l-initial CVC words aloud.
conceptual: Map each grapheme in a CVC word to its phoneme.
application: Repair /l/, vowel, or final-sound decoding errors.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why checking the middle vowel can repair a CVC reading error.
mixedReview: Mix /l/ CVC decoding with previously taught consonants.

formulaOrFactBank: CVC decoding = grapheme sounds in order + blend.
mistakeBasedRevision: If the word is wrong, isolate each sound again and reread the whole word.
weakTopicRevision: Practice fresh l-initial CVC words with the weakest vowel pattern.

activities.name: Sound-to-word mapping
steps: Show a taught l CVC word.

outcomes: Learner maps l to /l/ in print.
Learner decodes taught l CVC words accurately.
Learner blends left to right and self-corrects common errors.

Which word starts with l and has short /a/?
Which grapheme represents the /l/ sound at the start of “lip”?
Which word begins with the same sound as “log”?
Which word has l at the end?
What is the best way to decode “lug”?
A learner reads “lip” as “rip.” Which part should be checked first?
A learner reads “log” as “lag.” Which part needs checking?
Why should the learner look at every grapheme in a CVC word?
options: Each grapheme contributes to the word's sound sequence.
The final sound can be skipped.

questions.question: A learner can say /l/ but cannot blend /l/ /ɪ/ /p/. What is the best next practice?
options: Orally blend the sounds, then decode “lip” from print.

questions.question: After accurately decoding several taught /l/ CVC words, what should follow?
options: CVC spelling and controlled word-family reading
